reason: The text fragment (Exodus 1:6-12) is a narrative account of the death of Joseph, the rise of a new Pharaoh, and the beginning of Egyptian oppression of the Israelites. The passage contains no mention of Yahweh (God), religious practice, worship, or any portrayal of the Israelites as followers of God. The focus is entirely on the political and social dynamics between the Egyptian ruler and the Israelite population as ethnic/demographic groups, without any theological or religious content depicting them as worshippers of the God Yahweh.
